cases.text: Sampling-based MPC can satisfy predicted constraints yet become unsafe beyond its horizon, while barrier penalties can leave most rollouts with negligible importance weights. Neural Shield VIMPC addresses these failures through a learned discrete-time policy barrier and rollout resampling. The barrier approximates a policy's worst future constraint value to anticipate hazards beyond the horizon; resampling replaces unsafe states and control prefixes with safe counterparts when available, retaining control suffixes. With 500 trajectories, NS-MPPI had no crashes across tested Drone horizons, including ten steps. On AutoRally, a 12 m/s target speed, 15-step horizon and 30 trajectories per iteration yielded a crash rate of 0.04 versus S-MPPI's 0.46, at 73.64 Hz on a CPU. These findings support empirical safety, not a general guarantee: the barrier is unverified, and averaging feasible controls can violate nonconvex safety constraints.
cases.note: Distinguished horizon-related risk from sampling inefficiency, made resampling conditional on safe alternatives, and tied the empirical evidence to both limits on safety guarantees.

cases.text: An AutoRally comparison adding only resampling-based rollouts (RBR) to S-MPPI achieved comparable collision rates with roughly five times fewer trajectories over 100 trials, isolating the resampling benefit from barrier learning. Separately, with a 12 m/s target speed, 15-step horizon and 30 trajectories per optimization iteration, NS-MPPI's crash and collision rates were 0.04 and 0.06, versus 0.46 and 0.70 for S-MPPI; CPU control frequency decreased from 107.31 to 73.64 Hz. With 500 trajectories, NS-MPPI also had no crashes across tested Drone horizons, including ten steps. The barrier remains unverified.
cases.note: Separated the controlled resampling comparison from the full-controller results and stated the safety rates alongside the lower CPU control frequency.

cases.text: ArticuBot learns a hierarchical opening policy from simulated demonstrations. A weighted displacement model predicts grasping and opening subgoals as learned weighted averages of scene points plus offsets to four gripper landmarks. A diffusion controller conditions on these subgoals, object point clouds and end-effector states to generate opening actions. Training uses 42.3k trajectories over 322 objects. In a 200-object ablation without camera randomization, normalized opening, measured relative to demonstration opening, was 0.70 with the learned controller versus 0.24 with motion planning and IK-based control. Trained only on a simulated Franka, the policy opened 20 unseen real objects across Franka and X-Arm setups without real-world training. Deployment requires handles graspable from the fully closed state and target-object names for segmentation, but no articulation parameters. Weighted displacement's advantage is conditional: DP3 Transformer Diffusion performs better with all 322 training objects when neither training nor testing uses camera randomization.
cases.note: Clarified landmark aggregation, controller inputs, deployment assumptions and simulation-only transfer. Defined the opening measure and identified the exact camera condition that reverses the architecture comparison.

cases.text: With 200 training objects and no camera randomization, ArticuBot achieved normalized opening of 0.70 +/- 0.01, compared with 0.66 +/- 0.01 without per-point weights and 0.24 +/- 0.02 with motion planning and IK-based control replacing the learned controller. Values are means +/- standard deviations over three evaluation runs; the metric divides achieved joint-opening increase by the demonstration's increase, rather than measuring binary success. High-level comparisons held the low-level policy fixed. Weighted displacement outperformed the compared DP3 variants with camera-randomized training and testing, especially at camera poses outside the training distribution. However, DP3 Transformer Diffusion performed better with all 322 training objects when neither training nor testing used camera randomization.
cases.note: Defined normalized opening and its uncertainty, preserved the ablation conditions, and made both the fixed controller and camera-dependent reversal explicit.

cases.text: DemoGen augments spatial coverage for DP3 by transforming object-contact skills with objects, replanning intervening free-space motion, and consistently editing segmented point clouds and recorded proprioception. This avoids executing each synthetic trajectory but assumes reliable action execution using inverse-kinematics control with absolute end-effector targets. Across eight real-world tasks, task-averaged success increased from 11.0% with source-only training to 74.6% with DemoGen. Each task supplied one human demonstration and two recorded replays. Single-arm generation targeted kinematically verified evaluation configurations, adding nine perturbations within +/- 1.5 cm per planar axis for each target and source trajectory. Single-process synthetic generation took 0.010 seconds per trajectory, excluding collection and policy training. Spatial generalization remains limited because transformed single-view point clouds preserve previously visible surfaces rather than reconstructing newly exposed views, creating appearance mismatch at distant placements.
cases.note: Added the reliable-control assumption, aligned action and observation transformations, and qualified the real-world gain by source data, targeted placements and computation-only cost. Explained the single-view limitation.

cases.text: With DP3 training exposure matched by observation-action pair count, DemoGen achieved 88% task-averaged success across eight simulated tasks, versus 13% with one source trajectory and 91% with 25, using means over three seeds. Across eight real-world tasks, success averaged 74.6% versus 11.0% for the three-source-only baseline, with five repetitions per feasible configuration. Each task provided one human demonstration and two recorded replays. Single-arm generation targeted evaluated configurations with small perturbations; the bimanual task omitted perturbations. These gains do not establish unrestricted placement or viewpoint generalization: edited single-view point clouds retain originally visible surfaces, causing appearance mismatch and reduced performance farther from the source configuration.
cases.note: Clarified matched training exposure and seed averaging, connected the three real-world source trajectories to targeted evaluation placements, and explained why observed gains do not imply unrestricted generalization.
